reasoning_traces.think:
The core modeling approach leverages a modular architecture where the ball-carrier LSTM predicts expected yardage at each frame, conditioned on a rich set of tracking features including endzone-adjusted coordinates, relative geometry, and Voronoi-based spatial features. These predictions are then fed into an RFCDE (Random Forest Conditional Density Estimator) which computes the full conditional distribution of end-of-play yard lines. This distribution enables the calculation of expected points (EP) and win probability (WP) by integrating over the outcome space. The framework assumes that the ball-carrier's trajectory is Markovian and that the conditional density can be accurately estimated from the observed features. The model is trained on a subset of rushing plays from the NFL Big Data Bowl dataset, which provides high-frequency tracking data at 10 Hz. The LSTM architecture allows for temporal dependencies, while the RFCDE handles the probabilistic nature of outcomes. The system updates predictions at every frame, enabling real-time within-play valuation. Key assumptions include stationarity of play dynamics and sufficiency of the feature set. Failure modes arise when rare events like fumbles occur or when the model encounters novel play types not present in training data.
